title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十二: 賽典赤贍思丁 布魯海牙 高智耀 鐵哥
title.en: Volume 125 Biographies 12: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar, Buluhaiya, Gaozhiyao, Tiege
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十二: 賽典赤贍思丁 布魯海牙 高智耀 鐵哥 Volume 125 Biographies 12: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar, Buluhaiya, Gaozhiyao, Tiege

sentences.zh: 賽典赤贍思丁

translations.literal: Sayyid Ajall Shams al-Din
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall Shams al-Din

sentences.zh: 賽典赤贍思丁一名烏馬兒，回回人，別菴伯爾之裔。

translations.literal: Sayyid Ajall Shams al-Din had another name, Umar; he was a Muslim, a descendant of Bukhara.
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall Shams al-Din, also known as Umar, was a Muslim of Bukhara descent.

sentences.zh: 其國言賽典赤，猶華言貴族也。

translations.literal: In his country’s speech, sayyid ajall means, as in Chinese speech, noble.
translations.idiomatic: In his native tongue, sayyid ajall meant the same as “noble” in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，贍思丁率千騎以文豹白鶻迎降，命入宿衛，從征伐，以賽典赤呼之而不名。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned westward, Shams al-Din led a thousand horsemen to submit in welcome with patterned leopards and white gerfalcons; he was ordered into the palace guard, followed on campaigns, and was addressed as Sayyid Ajall rather than by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched west, Shams al-Din came to submit with a thousand riders, bringing tribute of patterned leopards and white gerfalcons. He was placed in the imperial guard and accompanied the campaigns; the court called him Sayyid Ajall instead of using his name.

sentences.zh: 七年，分鎮四川，宋將昝萬壽擁強兵守嘉定，與賽典赤軍對壘，一以誠意待之，不為侵掠，萬壽心服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was assigned to garrison Sichuan; the Song general Zan Wanshou held Jiading with a strong force and faced Sayyid Ajall’s army in camp; he treated him throughout with sincerity and made no raids, and Wanshou came to respect him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posted to Sichuan. The Song general Zan Wanshou held Jiading with a large army and faced Sayyid Ajall across the lines. Sayyid Ajall dealt with him in good faith and refrained from plunder, and Wanshou was won over.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賽典赤召還，萬壽請置酒為好，左右皆難之，賽典赤竟往不疑。

translations.literal: Before long Sayyid Ajall was recalled; Wanshou asked to set out wine in friendship; those at his side all found it difficult, yet Sayyid Ajall went in the end without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sayyid Ajall was recalled. Wanshou invited him to a farewell feast. His attendants all objected, but Sayyid Ajall went without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 酒至，左右復言未可飲，賽典赤笑曰：「若等何見之小耶。

translations.literal: When the wine arrived, those at his side again said he must not drink; Sayyid Ajall laughed and said, “You people—how small is your view!
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was served, his attendants again warned him not to drink. Sayyid Ajall laughed and said, “How narrow your thinking is!

sentences.zh: 咎將軍能毒我，其能盡毒我朝之人乎。」

translations.literal: General Zan may be able to poison me—can he poison every man of our court?”
translations.idiomatic: General Zan might poison me, but could he poison everyone in our army?”

sentences.zh: 萬壽嘆服。

translations.literal: Wanshou sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 八年，有旨：大軍見圍襄陽，各道宜進兵以牽制之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year there was an edict: the great army was now besieging Xiangyang; each route should advance troops to pin the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an order came down: with the main forces besieging Xiangyang, every command should advance troops to tie down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 於是賽典赤偕鄭鼎率兵水陸並進，至嘉定，獲宋將二人，順流縱筏，斷其浮橋，獲戰艦二十八艘。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sayyid Ajall together with Zheng Ding led troops forward by land and water; reaching Jiading, they captured two Song generals, sent rafts downstream, cut their pontoon bridge, and seized twenty-eight warships.
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall and Zheng Ding then advanced by land and water to Jiading, captured two Song generals, sent rafts downriver to destroy the pontoon bridge, and took twenty-eight warships.

sentences.zh: 尋命行省事于興元，專給糧餉。

translations.literal: Shortly he was ordered to conduct branch-secretariat affairs at Xingyuan, devoted solely to supplying grain and pay.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to handle branch-secretariat duties at Xingyuan, charged exclusively with provisioning grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝謂賽典赤曰：「雲南朕嘗親臨，比因委任失宜，使遠人不安，欲選謹厚者撫治之，無如卿者。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor said to Sayyid Ajall, “Yunnan I once visited in person; lately because appointments were ill chosen the distant peoples are unsettled. I wish to choose someone careful and steadfast to pacify and govern them—there is no one like you.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor told Sayyid Ajall, “I once campaigned in Yunnan myself. Recent misappointments have left the frontier peoples uneasy. I want a man of steady character to govern them—and no one suits better than you.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤拜受命，退朝，即訪求知雲南地理者，畫其山川城郭、驛舍軍屯、夷險遠近為圖以進，帝大悅，遂拜平章政事，行省雲南，賜鈔五十萬緡、金寶無筭。

translations.literal: Sayyid Ajall bowed and accepted the charge; after court he at once sought out those who knew Yunnan’s geography, drew mountains and rivers, walled cities, relay stations and military colonies, barbarian lands, difficult and easy terrain, and distances near and far into a map and presented it; the emperor was greatly pleased, and then appointed him Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, with a branch secretariat in Yunnan, granting five hundred thousand strings of paper money and gold and treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall bowed and accepted. After court he immediately found men who knew Yunnan’s terrain and had them map its mountains, cities, relay posts, garrisons, tribal districts, and routes—easy and hard, near and far—and presented the chart to the throne. The emperor was delighted and appointed him Grand Councillor of the Secretariat with authority over the Yunnan branch secretariat, granting five hundred thousand strings of paper money and untold gold and treasures.

sentences.zh: 時宗王脫忽魯方鎮雲南，惑於左右之言，以賽典赤至，必奪其權，具甲兵以為備。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial prince Tuohulur was stationed in Yunnan; misled by those at his side, he believed that when Sayyid Ajall arrived he would surely seize his power, and he readied armor and weapons as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prince Tuohulur was then governing Yunnan. His advisers convinced him that Sayyid Ajall had come to strip him of authority, and he armed his troops in preparation.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤聞之，乃遣其子納速剌丁先至王所，請曰：「天子以雲南守者非人，致諸國背叛，故命臣來安集之，且戒以至境即加撫循，今未敢專，願王遣一人來共議。」

translations.literal: When Sayyid Ajall heard of this, he sent his son Nasr al-Din ahead to the prince’s residence with a request: “The Son of Heaven, because Yunnan’s guardians were not the right men and caused the various states to rebel, therefore ordered me to come and settle them; he also admonished that upon reaching the border I must at once extend soothing care. Now I dare not act alone; I hope the prince will send one man to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Sayyid Ajall sent his son Nasr al-Din ahead to the prince with a message: “The emperor found Yunnan’s rulers unfit, which drove the peoples to revolt, and sent me to restore order. He charged me to begin conciliation the moment I arrived. I dare not act on my own—may Your Highness send someone to discuss matters with me.

sentences.zh: 王聞，遽罵其下曰：「吾幾為汝輩所誤。」

translations.literal: When the prince heard this, he at once reviled his subordinates, saying, “I was nearly led astray by you lot.
translations.idiomatic: The prince heard this and immediately rebuked his staff: “You nearly misled me.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣親臣撒滿、位哈乃等至，賽典赤問以何禮見，對曰：「吾等與納速剌丁偕來，視猶兄弟也，請用子禮見。」

translations.literal: The next day he sent close ministers Saman, Weihanai, and others. Sayyid Ajall asked with what rites he should receive them; they replied, “We came together with Nasr al-Din and regard you as a brother—please receive us with the rites due a son.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent his close advisers Saman, Weihanai, and others. Sayyid Ajall asked what ceremony they expected. They answered, “We came with Nasr al-Din and regard you as a brother—please receive us as a father would a son.

sentences.zh: 皆以名馬為贄，拜跪甚恭，觀者大駭。

translations.literal: Each presented famous horses as gifts and bowed and knelt with great respect; onlookers were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: They each offered fine horses as gifts and bowed and knelt with deep respect, astonishing all who watched.

sentences.zh: 乃設宴陳所賜金寶飲器，酒罷，盡以與之，二人大喜過望。

translations.literal: He then set out a banquet and displayed the gold, treasures, and drinking vessels the court had bestowed; when the wine ended, he gave them all away, and the two men rejoiced beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a feast and set out the gold, jewels, and drinking vessels the court had given him; when the banquet ended he gave them all to the two men, who were overwhelmed with joy.

sentences.zh: 明日來謝，語之曰：「二君雖為宗王親臣，未有名爵，不可以議國事，欲各授君行省斷事官，以未見王，未敢擅授。」

translations.literal: The next day they came to give thanks; he told them, “Although you two are the prince’s close ministers, you have no titles or ranks and may not deliberate on state affairs. I wish to appoint each of you branch-secretariat judicial officers, but because I have not yet seen the prince I dare not grant offices on my own.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they returned to thank him. He said, “You are the prince’s intimate advisers but hold no formal rank and may not discuss state affairs. I wish to appoint each of you judicial officers of the branch secretariat, but since I have not yet seen the prince I dare not do so without his approval.

sentences.zh: 令一人還，先稟王，王大悅。

translations.literal: He had one man return to report first to the prince; the prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He sent one of them back to report to the prince first. The prince was delighted.

sentences.zh: 由是政令一聽賽典赤所為。

translations.literal: From this all government orders were heard solely as Sayyid Ajall directed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on all administrative orders followed Sayyid Ajall’s authority alone.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏：「雲南諸夷未附者尚多，今擬宣慰司兼行元帥府事，並聽行省節制。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized: “Among Yunnan’s various Yi many are still unsubmitted; it is now proposed that the Pacification Commission also conduct marshal’s headquarters affairs, all subject to the branch secretariat’s control.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized: “Many tribal peoples in Yunnan remain unsubmitted. I propose that the Pacification Commission also exercise marshal’s authority, all under the branch secretariat’s direction.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「哈剌章、雲南壤地均也，而州縣皆以萬戶、千戶主之，宜改置令長。」

translations.literal: He further memorialized: “Karajang and Yunnan have equal territory, yet prefectures and counties are all ruled by myriarchs and chiliarchs; it is fitting to replace them with magistrates and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: “Karajang and Yunnan are comparable in territory, yet their prefectures and counties are governed by myriarchs and chiliarchs. They should be given regular magistrates and prefects instead.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以所改雲南郡縣上聞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he reported upward the Yunnan commanderies and counties he had reformed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he reported to the court the revised Yunnan prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 雲南俗無禮儀，男女往往自相配偶，親死則火之，不為喪祭。

translations.literal: Yunnan’s customs lacked ritual propriety; men and women often paired themselves on their own; when kin died they burned the bodies and performed no mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had no established ritual culture. Men and women often paired off on their own; when kin died the bodies were cremated and no mourning ceremonies were held.

sentences.zh: 無秔稻桑麻，子弟不知讀書。

translations.literal: They had no non-glutinous rice, mulberry, or hemp; their sons and younger brothers did not know how to read books.
translations.idiomatic: There was no cultivation of non-glutinous rice, mulberry, or hemp, and the young knew nothing of learning.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤教之拜跪之節，婚姻行媒，死者為之棺槨奠祭，教民播種，為陂池以備水旱，創建孔子廟、明倫堂，購經史，授學田，由是文風稍興。

translations.literal: Sayyid Ajall taught them the protocols of bowing and kneeling, marriage through go-betweens, coffins and burial offerings for the dead; he taught the people to sow seed, made embankment ponds to guard against flood and drought, founded a Temple of Confucius and a Hall of Illuminating Relationships, purchased classics and histories, and granted school fields—whereby literary culture gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall taught them bowing and kneeling etiquette, betrothal through matchmakers, and proper coffins and funeral rites for the dead. He taught the people to plant crops, built reservoirs against flood and drought, founded a Temple of Confucius and a Hall of Illuminating Relationships, purchased the classics and histories, and endowed school lands. From this a literary culture slowly took root.

sentences.zh: 雲南民以貝代錢，是時初行鈔法，民不便之，賽典赤為聞于朝，許仍其俗。

translations.literal: Yunnan’s people used shells in place of money; at this time paper currency was first implemented and the people found it inconvenient; Sayyid Ajall reported this to the court on their behalf, and permission was granted to continue their custom.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yunnan used cowrie shells as currency. When paper money was introduced they found it burdensome. Sayyid Ajall petitioned the court, and they were allowed to keep their old practice.

sentences.zh: 又患山路險遠，盜賊出沒，為行者病，相地置鎮，每鎮設土酋吏一人、百夫長一人，往來者或值劫掠，則罪及之。

translations.literal: He also grieved that mountain roads were perilous and remote and bandits appeared and vanished, which afflicted travelers; he chose sites to establish posts, and at each post set one native chieftain-official and one centurion; if travelers met robbery, punishment fell on them.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the danger of remote mountain roads where bandits lurked. He established guard posts along the routes, each staffed with a native official and a centurion who would be held responsible if travelers were robbed.

sentences.zh: 有土吏數輩，怨賽典赤不已，用至京師誣其專僭數事。

translations.literal: Several native officials, resenting Sayyid Ajall without end, went to the capital and falsely accused him of several acts of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Several native officials who bore endless grudges against Sayyid Ajall traveled to the capital and accused him of multiple acts of arrogation of authority.

sentences.zh: 帝顧侍臣曰：「賽典赤憂國愛民，朕洞知之，此輩何敢誣告！」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to attendant ministers and said, “Sayyid Ajall cares for the state and loves the people—I know this thoroughly; how dare this lot falsely accuse him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, “Sayyid Ajall cares for the realm and its people—I know him well. How dare these men slander him!

sentences.zh: 即命械送賽典赤處治之。

translations.literal: He at once ordered them shackled and sent to Sayyid Ajall for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them bound and sent back to Sayyid Ajall for punishment.

sentences.zh: 既至，脫其械，且諭之曰：「若曹不知上以便宜命我，故訴我專僭，我今不汝罪，且命汝以官，能竭忠自贖乎？」

translations.literal: When they arrived, he removed their shackles and moreover instructed them, saying, “You people did not know that the emperor empowered me at discretion, and therefore accused me of usurpation. Today I do not punish you; moreover I appoint you to office—can you exhaust loyalty and redeem yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived he had their bonds removed and told them, “You did not know the emperor had given me discretionary authority, so you accused me of overstepping. I will not punish you now; I will even give you office. Can you serve faithfully and redeem yourselves?

sentences.zh: 皆叩頭拜謝曰：「某有死罪，平章既生之而又官之，誓以死報。」

translations.literal: All knocked their heads and bowed in thanks, saying, “We deserved death; the Grand Councillor has given us life and moreover office—we vow to repay with our lives.”
translations.idiomatic: They all kowtowed and said, “We deserved death. You have spared us and given us office—we swear to repay you with our lives.”

sentences.zh: 交趾叛服不常，湖廣省發兵屢征不利，賽典赤遣人諭以逆順禍福，且約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi’s submission and rebellion were inconstant; Huguang Province sent troops repeatedly to campaign without success; Sayyid Ajall sent men to instruct them in the consequences of rebellion and loyalty, and moreover pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi’s loyalty was erratic. Huguang Province had sent troops repeatedly without success. Sayyid Ajall sent envoys to explain the consequences of rebellion and loyalty and proposed a bond of brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 交趾王大喜，親至雲南，賽典赤郊迎，待以賓禮，遂乞永為藩臣。

translations.literal: The king of Jiaozhi was greatly pleased, came in person to Yunnan; Sayyid Ajall met him in the suburbs and received him with guest rites; he then begged to be a vassal forever.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Jiaozhi was delighted and came in person to Yunnan. Sayyid Ajall met him outside the city and received him as an honored guest. The king then asked to remain a vassal permanently.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃甸叛，往征之，有憂色，從者問故，賽典赤曰：「吾非憂出征也，憂汝曹冒鋒鏑，不幸以無辜而死；

translations.literal: Luopan district rebelled; he went to campaign against it with a troubled look; followers asked the reason; Sayyid Ajall said, “I do not worry about going on campaign—I worry that you will brave blades and arrows and by misfortune die though innocent;
translations.idiomatic: When Luopan district rebelled he set out to suppress it with a troubled expression. His attendants asked why. Sayyid Ajall said, “I am not worried about the campaign itself—I worry that you will face the blades and die though innocent;

sentences.zh: 又憂汝曹劫虜平民，使不聊生，及民叛，則又從而征之耳。」

translations.literal: I also worry that you will plunder and seize common people, leaving them with no livelihood; and when the people rebel, we must campaign against them again.”
translations.idiomatic: and I worry that you will plunder civilians and leave them destitute—so that when the people rebel we must campaign again.”

sentences.zh: 師次蘿槃城，三日不降，諸將請攻之，賽典赤不可，遣使以理諭之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Luopan city; for three days they did not submit; the generals asked to attack; Sayyid Ajall would not allow it and sent envoys to instruct them with reason.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Luopan city. After three days without surrender the generals asked to attack, but Sayyid Ajall refused and sent envoys to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃主曰：「謹奉命。」

translations.literal: The lord of Luopan said, “I respectfully accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Luopan said, “I respectfully obey.

sentences.zh: 越三日又不降，諸將奮勇請進兵，賽典赤又不可。

translations.literal: After three more days they still did not submit; the generals eagerly asked to advance; Sayyid Ajall again would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later they still had not submitted. The generals eagerly pressed to advance, but Sayyid Ajall again refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而將卒有乘城進攻者，賽典赤大怒，遽鳴金止之，召萬戶叱責之曰：「天子命我安撫雲南，未嘗命以殺戮也。

translations.literal: Before long officers and soldiers mounted the wall to attack; Sayyid Ajall was greatly angered, hastily sounded the gong to stop them, summoned the myriarch, and rebuked him, saying, “The Son of Heaven ordered me to pacify Yunnan—he never ordered slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon some soldiers scaled the walls to attack. Sayyid Ajall was furious. He sounded the gong to halt them and summoned the myriarch. “The emperor sent me to pacify Yunnan,” he rebuked him, “not to slaughter.

sentences.zh: 無主將命而擅攻，於軍法當誅。」

translations.literal: To attack without the commander’s order—under military law you should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: To attack without your commander’s order is a capital offense under military law.

sentences.zh: 命左右縛之，諸將叩首，請俟城下之日從事。

translations.literal: He ordered those at his side to bind him; the generals knocked their heads and asked to wait until the day the city fell to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to bind the officer. The generals kowtowed and begged to defer punishment until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃主聞之曰：「平章寬仁如此，吾拒命不祥。」

translations.literal: When the lord of Luopan heard this he said, “The Grand Councillor is so generous and humane—my defiance is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord of Luopan heard this he said, “The Grand Councillor is so merciful—resistance would be ill-fated.

sentences.zh: 乃舉國出降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole state came out to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then surrendered with his entire domain.

sentences.zh: 將卒亦釋不誅。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were also released and not executed.
translations.idiomatic: The offending officers and soldiers were released without punishment.

sentences.zh: 由是西南諸夷翕然款附。

translations.literal: From this the various Yi of the southwest came forward in unity to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From this the tribal peoples of the southwest submitted in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 夷酋每來見，例有所獻納，賽典赤悉分賜從官，或以給貧民，秋毫無所私；

translations.literal: Whenever tribal chiefs came to see him, by custom there were offerings presented; Sayyid Ajall divided them all among following officials, or gave them to poor commoners, keeping not the slightest for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tribal chiefs visited they brought customary gifts. Sayyid Ajall distributed everything among his staff or gave it to the poor, keeping nothing for himself;

sentences.zh: 為酒食勞酋長，製衣冠襪履，易其卉服草履。

translations.literal: he set out wine and food to refresh the chiefs, made caps, robes, socks, and shoes, and exchanged them for their wild dress and grass sandals.
translations.idiomatic: he feasted the chiefs, provided caps, robes, socks, and shoes, and replaced their rough tribal dress and grass sandals.

sentences.zh: 酋皆感悅。

translations.literal: The chiefs were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 子五人：長納速剌丁；

translations.literal: He had five sons: the eldest, Nasr al-Din;
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. The eldest was Nasr al-Din;

sentences.zh: 次哈散，廣東道宣慰使都元帥；

translations.literal: next Husain, Pacification Commissioner and Grand Marshal of the Guangdong Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: next Husain, Pacification Commissioner and Grand Marshal of the Guangdong Circuit;

sentences.zh: 次忽辛；

translations.literal: next Huxin;
translations.idiomatic: next Huxin;

sentences.zh: 次苫速丁兀默里，建昌路緫管；

translations.literal: next Shams al-Din Umarli, Surveillance Commissioner of Jianchang Route;
translations.idiomatic: next Shams al-Din Umarli, chief administrator of Jianchang Route;

sentences.zh: 次馬速忽，雲南諸路行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: next Masuhu, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat of the Secretariat for all routes.
translations.idiomatic: and youngest Masuhu, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁，累官中奉大夫、雲南諸路宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: Nasr al-Din, through successive offices reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pacification Commissioner and Grand Marshal of all Yunnan routes.
translations.idiomatic: Nasr al-Din rose through the ranks to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Pacification Commissioner and Grand Marshal of all Yunnan routes.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，遷帥大理，以軍抵金齒、蒲、驃、曲蠟、緬國，招安夷寨三百，籍戶十二萬二百，定租賦，置郵傳，立衛兵，歸以馴象十二入貢，有旨賞金五十兩、衣二襲，麾下士賞銀有差。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to command Dali; with troops he reached Jinchi, Pu, Piao, Quwax, and Burma, pacified three hundred Yi stockades, registered 120,200 households, fixed rents and levies, established courier posts, set up guards, and on return presented twelve tame elephants as tribute; an edict rewarded fifty taels of gold and two suits of clothing, and soldiers under his command were rewarded with silver in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 16 he was transferred to command Dali. He led troops to Jinchi, Pu, Piao, Quwax, and Burma, pacified three hundred tribal stockades, registered 120,200 households, fixed taxes and levies, established courier posts, and raised garrisons. He returned with twelve tame elephants as tribute. The court rewarded him with fifty taels of gold and two suits of clothing; his officers and men received silver in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 會其父贍思丁歿，雲南省臣於諸夷失撫綏之方，世祖憂之，近臣以納速剌丁為言。

translations.literal: It happened that his father Shams al-Din died; the Yunnan provincial ministers lost the methods of soothing and binding the various Yi; Shizu was troubled; close ministers spoke on behalf of Nasr al-Din.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Shams al-Din died, the Yunnan provincial officials lost control over the tribal peoples. Kublai was concerned, and his close advisers recommended Nasr al-Din.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授資德大夫、雲南行中書省左丞，尋陞右丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Virtuous Grand Master and Left Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat; shortly he was promoted to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Virtuous Grand Master and Left Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, and soon promoted to Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 建言三事：其一謂雲南省規措所造金簿貿易病民，宜罷；

translations.literal: He offered counsel on three matters: the first said that the gold ledgers for trade devised by Yunnan Province harmed the people and should be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed three reforms. First, the gold-account trade system devised by Yunnan Province burdened the people and should be abolished;

sentences.zh: 其一謂雲南有省，有宣慰司，又有都元帥府，近宣慰司已奏罷，而元帥府尚存，臣謂行省既兼領軍民，則元帥府亦在所當罷；

translations.literal: the second said that Yunnan had a province, a Pacification Commission, and also a Grand Marshal’s headquarters; recently the Pacification Commission had been memorialized for abolition while the marshal’s headquarters still remained—I hold that since the branch secretariat already commands both military and civil affairs, the marshal’s headquarters should also be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: second, Yunnan had a branch secretariat, a Pacification Commission, and a Grand Marshal’s headquarters; the Pacification Commission had recently been abolished but the marshal’s headquarters remained—since the branch secretariat already governed both civil and military affairs, the marshal’s headquarters should go as well;

sentences.zh: 其一謂雲南官員子弟入質，臣謂達官子弟當遣，餘宜罷。

translations.literal: the third said that sons of Yunnan officials were sent as hostages to court—I hold that sons of high officials should be sent, but the rest should cease.
translations.idiomatic: third, regarding hostages from Yunnan official families sent to court—only sons of senior officials should remain; the rest should be discontinued.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorials were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進榮祿大夫、平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was advanced to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奏減合剌章冗官，歲省俸金九百餘兩；

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce redundant officials in Karajang, saving more than nine hundred taels of salary gold per year;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to cut redundant posts in Karajang, saving more than nine hundred taels of salary gold annually;

sentences.zh: 屯田課程專人掌之，歲得五千兩。

translations.literal: garrison-field revenues were placed under dedicated managers, yielding five thousand taels per year.
translations.idiomatic: and placed garrison-field revenues under dedicated managers, yielding five thousand taels per year.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以合剌章蒙古軍千人，從皇太子脫歡征交趾，論功賞銀二千兩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with one thousand Mongol troops of Karajang, he followed Crown Prince Togan in campaigning against Jiaozhi; for merit he was rewarded two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he led one thousand Karajang Mongol troops with Crown Prince Togan against Jiaozhi and was rewarded two thousand taels of silver for his service.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，進拜陝西行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was advanced and appointed Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠佐理協德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、中書左丞相，封延安王。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title Merit Subject Who Sincerely Assists in Ordering and Harmonizes Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the privilege of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Left Chief Councillor of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan’an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Merit Subject Who Sincerely Assists in Ordering and Harmonizes Virtue, Grand Preceptor, with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and Left Chief Councillor of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan’an.

sentences.zh: 子十二人：伯顏，中書平章政事；

translations.literal: He had twelve sons: Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons: Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 烏馬兒，江浙行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Umar, Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Umar, Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 劄法兒，荊湖宣慰使；

translations.literal: Zafar, Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu;
translations.idiomatic: Zafar, Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu;

sentences.zh: 忽先，雲南行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Husain (Huxian), Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Huxian, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 沙的，雲南行省左丞；

translations.literal: Sadi, Left Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Sadi, Left Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 阿容，太常禮儀院使；

translations.literal: Arong, Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Arong, Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 伯顏察兒，中書平章政事，佩金虎符，贈太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、中書左丞相、奉元王，諡忠憲。

translations.literal: Bayancha’er, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, wearing the golden tiger tally; posthumously Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with privilege of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Left Chief Councillor of the Secretariat, Prince of Fengyuan; posthumous title Loyal and Law-abiding.
translations.idiomatic: Bayancha’er, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, bearer of the golden tiger tally; posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Left Chief Councillor of the Secretariat, and Prince of Fengyuan, with the posthumous title Loyal and Law-abiding.

sentences.zh: 忽辛，至元初以世臣子備宿衛，世祖善其應對。

translations.literal: Huxin, in the early Zhiyuan period as son of a hereditary minister served in the palace guard; Shizu approved his replies.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin, as the son of a hereditary minister, served in the palace guard in the early Zhiyuan period. Kublai admired his ready wit.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14 he was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為河南等路宣慰司同知。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Associate Pacification Commissioner of the Henan and other circuits Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as Associate Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 河南多強盜，往往群聚山林，劫殺行路，官軍收捕失利，忽辛以招安自任，遣土豪持檄諭之。

translations.literal: Henan had many fierce bandits who often gathered in groups in mountains and forests, robbed and killed travelers on the roads; government troops in pursuit and capture met with failure; Huxin took winning them over by appeasement as his own charge and sent local strongmen bearing proclamations to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had many bandits who gathered in the hills to rob travelers. Government troops had failed to suppress them. Huxin took on the task of winning them over and sent local leaders with proclamations to persuade them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊二人來自歸，忽辛賜之冠巾，且諭之曰：「汝昔為賊，今既自歸，即良民矣。」

translations.literal: Before long two bandits came of themselves to submit; Huxin bestowed caps and scarves on them and moreover instructed them, saying, “You were once bandits; now that you have submitted of yourselves, you are good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two bandits surrendered voluntarily. Huxin gave them caps and scarves and told them, “You were bandits; now that you have come in, you are honest subjects.

sentences.zh: 俾侍左右，出入房闥無間，悉放還，令遍諭其黨。

translations.literal: He had them attend at his left and right; entering and leaving the inner chambers without barrier, he released them all and ordered them to instruct their fellows everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He kept them at his side, letting them come and go freely from his private quarters, then sent them back to spread the word among their comrades.

sentences.zh: 數日後，招集其為首者十輩來，身長各七尺餘，羅拜庭下，顧視異常，衆悉驚怖失措。

translations.literal: Several days later he summoned ten of their leaders to come; each was over seven chi in height; they bowed in a row below the hall; looking about they were extraordinary; the crowd was all frightened and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he summoned ten of their leaders. Each stood over seven feet tall. They bowed in a row in the courtyard, their appearance so striking that everyone present was terrified.

sentences.zh: 忽辛命吏籍其姓名為民，俾隨侍左右，夜則令卧戶外，時呼而飲食之，各得其歡心。

translations.literal: Huxin ordered clerks to register their names as commoners, had them follow and attend at his left and right; at night he had them sleep outside the door; from time to time he called them to eat and drink; each obtained his pleased heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin had their names registered as commoners and kept them at his side. At night he had them sleep outside his door, called them in for food and drink, and won each man’s trust.

sentences.zh: 群盜聞之，相繼款附。

translations.literal: When bandit groups heard of this, they came forward in succession to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread, bandits surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授雲南諸路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Transport Commissioner of all Yunnan routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Transport Commissioner for all Yunnan routes.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉陝西道。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the Shaanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 又明年，授燕南河北道宣慰司同知，尋除南京緫管。

translations.literal: The year after that he was appointed Associate Pacification Commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit; shortly he was removed and made Chief Administrator of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he became Associate Pacification Commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Circuit, and soon afterward chief administrator of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授兩浙鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，進江東道宣慰使，改陝西行臺御史中丞，再改雲南行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade he was advanced to Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangdong Circuit, changed to Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, and again changed to Right Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 9 he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangdong Circuit, then transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, and again to Right Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既至，條具諸不便事言于宗王，請更張之，王不可，忽辛與左丞劉正馳還京師，有旨令宗王協力施行。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he itemized various inconvenient matters and spoke of them to the imperial prince, requesting thorough reform; the prince would not agree; Huxin together with Left Vice Director Liu Zheng galloped back to the capital; an edict ordered the prince to cooperate in carrying them out.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he listed abuses to the imperial prince and asked for reform. The prince refused. Huxin and Left Vice Director Liu Zheng rode posthaste to the capital. An edict ordered the prince to cooperate in implementing the reforms.

sentences.zh: 由是一切病民之政，悉革而新之。

translations.literal: From this all policies that afflicted the people were entirely reformed and made new.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every policy that harmed the people was abolished and replaced.

sentences.zh: 豪民規避徭役，往往投充王府宿衛，有司不勝供給，忽辛按朝廷元額所無者，悉籍為民，去其宿衛三分之二。

translations.literal: Powerful commoners evading corvée and levies often enrolled themselves as palace-guard retainers of the princely establishment; the responsible offices could not bear the supply burden; Huxin investigated those beyond the court’s original quotas and registered them all as commoners, removing two-thirds of the palace-guard retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men often evaded labor levies by enrolling as palace-guard retainers of the princely establishment, overwhelming local offices. Huxin investigated those beyond the court’s authorized quotas, registered them as commoners, and cut the princely guard rolls by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 馬龍州酋謀叛，陰與外賊通，持所受宣敕納賊以示信，事覺，宗王為左右所蔽，將釋不問，忽辛與劉正反覆研鞫，反狀盡得，竟斬之。

translations.literal: The chief of Malong prefecture plotted rebellion, secretly communicating with outside bandits; he held the patent and edict he had received and gave it to bandits to show trust; when the matter was discovered, the imperial prince was screened by those at his side and was about to release him without inquiry; Huxin and Liu Zheng repeatedly examined and interrogated until the facts of rebellion were fully obtained, and in the end he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of Malong prefecture plotted rebellion and secretly contacted outside bandits, giving them his official patent as a pledge of alliance. When the plot was exposed the prince’s advisers shielded him and were about to let him go. Huxin and Liu Zheng investigated thoroughly, proved the treason, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 軍糧支給，地理遠近不同，吏夤緣為姦，忽辛籍軍戶姓名及倉廩處所，為更番支給，吏姦始除。

translations.literal: For army grain disbursement, geography near and far differed; clerks used connections to commit fraud; Huxin registered military household names and granary locations and arranged rotation in disbursement; clerical fraud was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Army grain was issued according to distance, and clerks exploited the system for profit. Huxin registered military households and granary locations and instituted a rotating schedule of disbursement, ending the clerks’ abuses.

sentences.zh: 先是，贍思丁為雲南平章時，建孔子廟為學校，撥田五頃，以供祭祀教養。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shams al-Din was Grand Councillor in Yunnan, he built a Temple of Confucius as a school and allotted five qing of fields to supply sacrifices and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shams al-Din served as Grand Councillor in Yunnan, he had built a Temple of Confucius as a school and set aside five qing of land for sacrifices and instruction.

sentences.zh: 贍思丁卒，田為大德寺所有，忽辛按廟學舊籍奪歸之。

translations.literal: When Shams al-Din died, the fields came into the possession of the Dade Temple; Huxin investigated the temple-school’s old registers and seized them back.
translations.idiomatic: After Shams al-Din’s death the land passed to the Dade Temple. Huxin consulted the temple-school records and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 乃復下諸郡邑遍立廟學，選文學之士為之教官，文風大興。

translations.literal: He then again ordered all commanderies and districts to establish temple-schools everywhere, chose men of literary learning as their instructors, and literary culture flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every prefecture and district to establish temple-schools, appointed scholars as instructors, and literary culture flourished.

sentences.zh: 王府畜馬繁多，悉縱之郊，敗民禾稼，而牧人又在民家宿食，室無寧居。

translations.literal: The princely establishment kept many horses and turned them all loose in the suburbs, ruining the people’s grain crops; moreover the herdsmen lodged and ate in commoners’ homes, and households had no peaceful dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The princely establishment kept many horses and pastured them in the suburbs, trampling the people’s crops. Herdsmen lodged and ate in private homes, leaving households in constant turmoil.

sentences.zh: 忽辛度地置草場，搆屋數十間，使為牧所，民得以安。

translations.literal: Huxin surveyed land and set up pasture grounds, built several tens of rooms, and made them herding stations, so the people could be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin selected sites for pastures, built several dozen buildings as herding stations, and the people were left in peace.

sentences.zh: 廣南酋沙奴素強悍，宋時嘗賜以金印，雲南諸部悉平，獨此梗化。

translations.literal: The Guangnan chief Shanü had always been fierce and strong; in Song times he had been granted a golden seal; all Yunnan’s divisions were pacified, but this alone resisted transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangnan chief Shanü had long been fierce and defiant. The Song had once granted him a golden seal. All other Yunnan districts had submitted, but he alone held out.

sentences.zh: 忽辛遣使誘致，待之以禮，留數月不遣，酋請還，忽辛曰：「汝欲還，可納印來。」

translations.literal: Huxin sent envoys to entice him to come; he received him with ritual courtesy and detained him for several months without sending him back; the chief asked to return; Huxin said, “If you wish to return, you may surrender the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin sent envoys to lure him in and received him with courtesy. He detained him for months. When the chief asked to return, Huxin said, “If you wish to go home, surrender your seal.

sentences.zh: 酋不得已，齎印以納，忽辛置酒宴勞，諷令偕印入覲，帝大悅。

translations.literal: The chief had no choice; he brought the seal and submitted it; Huxin set out wine to feast and refresh him, and tactfully had him enter audience with the seal; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief had no choice but to bring the seal and submit it. Huxin feasted him and tactfully sent him to court with the seal. The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，緬國主負固不臣，忽辛遣人諭之曰：「我老賽典赤平章子也，惟先訓是遵，凡官府於汝國所不便事，當一切為汝更之。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, the lord of Burma stubbornly refused submission; Huxin sent men to instruct him, saying, “I am the son of the old Sayyid Ajall, Grand Councillor; I follow only our forefathers’ teaching—whatever in your state the government finds inconvenient, I shall entirely change it for you.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 5 the king of Burma stubbornly refused to submit. Huxin sent envoys who told him, “I am the son of the late Sayyid Ajall, Grand Councillor. I follow my father’s ways. Whatever policies of ours burden your kingdom, I will change them all for you.

sentences.zh: 緬國主聞之，遂與使者偕來，獻白象一，且曰：「此象古來所未有，今聖德所致，敢效方物。」

translations.literal: When the lord of Burma heard this, he then came together with the envoys, presented one white elephant, and said, “This elephant has never existed since antiquity; it is brought forth by present sagely virtue—I dare offer it as local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the king of Burma came with the envoys, presented a white elephant, and said, “Such an elephant has never been seen before. It is a gift of the emperor’s virtue, and I offer it as tribute.

sentences.zh: 既入，帝賜緬國主以世子之號。

translations.literal: After he entered, the emperor bestowed on the lord of Burma the title of heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival the emperor granted the king of Burma the title of imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 烏蠻等租賦，歲發軍徵索乃集，忽辛以利害榜諭諸蠻，不遣一卒，而租賦咸足。

translations.literal: Rent and levies of the Wuman and others were collected only after dispatching troops each year to demand them; Huxin posted notices on benefits and harms to instruct the various Man, sent not a single soldier, and yet rent and levies were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from the Wuman and other tribes had required annual military collection. Huxin posted notices explaining the consequences of compliance and defiance, sent not a single soldier, and collected the full levy.

sentences.zh: 俄有為飛語及符讖以惑宗王者，忽辛引劉正密為奏馳報，朝廷遣使臨問，凡造言之徒悉誅之，忽辛偕使者還覲。

translations.literal: Before long someone spread rumors and prognostications to confuse the imperial prince; Huxin drew Liu Zheng aside to memorialize in secret and report posthaste; the court sent envoys to investigate on the spot; all who fabricated words were executed; Huxin returned with the envoys to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rumors and prophecies spread to unsettle the imperial prince. Huxin and Liu Zheng secretly memorialized the court. Envoys were sent to investigate, all who had spread the slander were executed, and Huxin returned to court with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，出為四川行省左丞，改江浙行省。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade he went out as Left Vice Director of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and was changed to the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 8 he was posted as Left Vice Director of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，拜榮祿大夫、江西行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，以母老謝職歸養。

translations.literal: The next year, because his mother was old, he resigned his post to return and support her.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he resigned to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 又明年正月卒。

translations.literal: The year after, in the first month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following first month.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，贈守德宣惠敏政功臣、上柱國、雍國公，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was posthumously given the title Merit Subject Who Guards Virtue, Proclaims Grace, and Is Keen in Governance, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Yong, with posthumous title Loyal and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 he was posthumously honored as Merit Subject Who Guards Virtue, Proclaims Grace, and Is Keen in Governance, Upper Pillar of the State, and Duke of Yong, with the posthumous title Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子二人：伯杭，中慶路達魯花赤；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Bohang, Darughachi of Zhongqing Route;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Bohang, Darughachi of Zhongqing Route;

sentences.zh: 曲列，湖南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: Qulie, Pacification Commissioner of the Hunan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: and Qulie, Pacification Commissioner of the Hunan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙

translations.literal: Buluhaiya
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙，畏吾人也。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was a man of the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya was a Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 祖牙兒八海牙，父吉臺海牙，俱以功為其國世臣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ya’erbahaiya and his father Jitaihaiya both, through merit, were hereditary ministers of their state.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ya’erbahaiya and his father Jitaihaiya had both become hereditary ministers of their state through merit.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙幼孤，依舅氏家就學，未幾，即善其國書，尤精騎射。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was orphaned young; he relied on his mother’s family’s house to pursue study; before long he was skilled in his state’s script and especially excelled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Buluhaiya studied at his uncle’s home. He soon mastered the Uyghur script and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 年十八，隨其主內附，充宿衛。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he followed his lord in submitting inward and served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he accompanied his lord in submitting to the dynasty and joined the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，布魯海牙扈從，不避勞苦，帝嘉其勤，賜以羊馬氈帳，又以居里可汗女石抹氏配之。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned westward, Buluhaiya attended and followed, not shunning hardship; the emperor praised his diligence and bestowed sheep, horses, and felt tents; moreover he matched him with Lady Shimò, daughter of the Jürki Khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched west, Buluhaiya followed without shirking hardship. The emperor praised his diligence and rewarded him with sheep, horses, and felt tents, and gave him Lady Shimò, daughter of the Jürki Khan, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，諸王來會，選使燕京緫理財幣。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, the princes came to assemble; he was chosen as envoy to Yanjing to oversee finances and currency in general.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu’s death the princes assembled, and Buluhaiya was chosen as envoy to Yanjing to manage finances.

sentences.zh: 使還，莊聖太后聞其廉謹，以名求之於太宗，凡中宮軍民匠戶之在燕京、中山者，悉命統之，又賜以中山店舍園田、民戶二十，授真定路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Empress Zhuangsheng heard of his integrity and prudence and sought him by name from Taizong; all palace military, civil, and artisan households in Yanjing and Zhongshan were ordered under his command; he was further granted Zhongshan shops, dwellings, garden fields, and twenty commoner households, and appointed Darughachi of Zhending Route.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Empress Zhuangsheng, hearing of his integrity, requested him by name from Ögedei. All palace military, civil, and artisan households in Yanjing and Zhongshan were placed under his command. He was granted shops, gardens, and twenty households in Zhongshan and appointed Darughachi of Zhending Route.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，拜燕南諸路廉訪使，佩金虎符，賜民戶十。

translations.literal: In the xinmao year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of all Yannan routes, wore the golden tiger tally, and was granted ten commoner households.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinmao year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of all Yannan routes, given the golden tiger tally, and granted ten households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授斷事官，使職如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed judicial officer, his envoy duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also appointed judicial officer while retaining his previous duties.

sentences.zh: 時斷事官得專生殺，多倚勢作威，而布魯海牙小心謹密，慎於用刑。

translations.literal: At that time judicial officers could decide life and death on their own; many relied on power to make might; but Buluhaiya was careful and prudent and cautious in applying punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officers then held power of life and death, and many abused their authority. Buluhaiya was careful and restrained in imposing punishments.

sentences.zh: 有民誤毆人死，吏論以重法，其子號泣請代死，布魯海牙戒吏，使擒于市，懼則殺之。

translations.literal: A commoner mistakenly beat a man to death; clerks argued for the heavy law; his son wailed and begged to die in his stead; Buluhaiya warned the clerks and had him seized in the market—if afraid, then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: A man accidentally beat someone to death. The clerks sought the death penalty. His son wept and begged to die in his father’s place. Buluhaiya told the clerks to seize the son in the market and execute him if he showed fear.

sentences.zh: 既而不懼，乃曰：「誤毆人死，情有可宥，子而能孝，義無可誅。」

translations.literal: When he was not afraid, he then said, “Mistakenly beating a man to death—there is circumstance for pardon; the son who can be filial—righteousness gives no grounds for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the son showed no fear, Buluhaiya said, “Accidental killing admits of mercy, and a son who would die for his father cannot be punished.

sentences.zh: 遂併釋之，使出銀以資葬埋，且呼死者家諭之，其人悅從。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released them both, had them produce silver to fund burial, and moreover summoned the dead man’s family to instruct them; those people gladly obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He released them both, had them pay silver for the burial, and summoned the victim’s family to explain. They accepted willingly.

sentences.zh: 是時法制未定，奴有罪者，主得專殺，布魯海牙知其非法而不能救，嘗出金贖死者數十人。

translations.literal: At that time the legal system was not fixed; when slaves had offenses, masters could kill them outright; Buluhaiya knew this was unlawful but could not save them; he once paid gold to redeem several tens of the condemned.
translations.idiomatic: The law was not yet settled, and masters could kill offending slaves at will. Buluhaiya knew this was wrong but could not stop it; he once paid gold to redeem dozens of condemned slaves.

sentences.zh: 征討之際，隸軍籍者，憚於行役，往往募人代之，又軍中多逃歸者，朝廷下制：募代者杖百，逃歸者死。

translations.literal: During campaigns, those on military registers dreaded corvée and often hired men to replace them; moreover in the armies many fled home; the court issued regulations: those who hired substitutes—one hundred strokes; those who fled home—death.
translations.idiomatic: During campaigns men on the military rolls often hired substitutes rather than serve. Many soldiers also deserted. The court decreed one hundred strokes for hiring substitutes and death for deserters.

sentences.zh: 命布魯海牙與斷事官卜只兒按順天等路，及至州縣，得募人代者萬一千戶、逃者十二人。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya and judicial officer Bozhier were ordered to investigate Shuntian and other circuits; reaching prefectures and counties, they found those who had hired substitutes—eleven thousand one hundred households—and deserters—twelve men.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya and the judicial officer Bozhier were ordered to investigate Shuntian and other circuits. In the prefectures and counties they found eleven thousand one hundred households that had hired substitutes and twelve deserters.

sentences.zh: 然募者聞命將下，已潛遣家人易代募者，布魯海牙聞之，歎曰：「募者已懼罪往易，逃者因單弱思歸，情皆可矜，吾可不伸理耶。」

translations.literal: Yet when those who had hired substitutes heard the order was about to be issued, they had already secretly sent family members to replace the hired men; when Buluhaiya heard this, he sighed and said, “Those who hired substitutes, fearing guilt, sent others to take their place; deserters, because they were weak and alone, wished to return home—the circumstances of all may be pitied—how can I not seek justice for them?
translations.idiomatic: Learning that families had secretly sent relatives to take the place of hired substitutes, Buluhaiya sighed and said, “Those who hired substitutes acted from fear of punishment, and deserters fled because they were weak and homesick. Both deserve mercy. How can I not plead their case?

sentences.zh: 遂奏其狀，皆得輕減。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized the facts, and all received lighter reduction.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the facts, and all received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 有丁多產富而家人不往，及未至役所而即逃者，則曰：「此而不殺，何以戒後！」

translations.literal: When there were many adult sons, rich estates, yet family members who would not go, or those who fled before reaching the service post, he would say, “If these are not killed, how can later cases be warned!
translations.idiomatic: But when wealthy families with many sons refused to serve, or men fled before reaching their posts, he said, “If these are not punished, how will others be deterred?

sentences.zh: 有竊妓逃者，吏論當死，布魯海牙曰：「敗亂綱常，罪固宜死；

translations.literal: There was one who stole a courtesan and fled; clerks argued he should die; Buluhaiya said, “To corrupt and overturn the constant bonds—death is indeed fitting;
translations.idiomatic: When a man who had abducted a courtesan was sentenced to death, Buluhaiya said, “Disrupting moral order deserves death—

sentences.zh: 此妓也，豈可例論！」

translations.literal: but this was a courtesan—how can the same rule apply!
translations.idiomatic: but she was a courtesan. The same rule cannot apply!

sentences.zh: 命杖之。

translations.literal: He ordered him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him flogged instead.

sentences.zh: 其執法平允類如此。

translations.literal: His enforcement of law with fair balance was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His even-handed justice was of this kind throughout.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙性孝友，造大宅於燕京，自畏吾國迎母來居，事之，得祿不入私室。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya’s nature was filial and brotherly; he built a great residence in Yanjing, welcomed his mother from the Uyghur state to dwell there, served her, and salary he received did not enter his private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya was filial and devoted to kin. He built a large house in Yanjing and brought his mother from the Uyghur lands to live there. He served her devotedly and never kept his salary for himself.

sentences.zh: 幼時叔父阿里普海牙欺之，盡有其產，及貴顯，築室宅旁，迎阿里普海牙居之，弟益特思海牙以宿憾為言，常慰諭之，終無間言。

translations.literal: In youth his uncle Alipuhaiya had cheated him and taken all his property; when he became noble and eminent, he built a house beside his residence and welcomed Alipuhaiya to dwell there; his younger brother Yitesihaiya spoke of old resentments, but he constantly comforted and instructed him, and in the end there was no estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his uncle Alipuhaiya had cheated him out of his inheritance. When he rose to prominence he built a house beside his own and welcomed his uncle to live there. His younger brother Yitesihaiya spoke of old grievances, but Buluhaiya always soothed him, and they remained without estrangement.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜以太府綾絹五千匹，絲絮相等，弟求四之一納其國賦，盡與之，無吝色。

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed five thousand bolts of palace damask and an equal amount of silk floss; his younger brother asked for one quarter to pay their state’s levy; he gave it all, with no sign of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once granted him five thousand bolts of palace silk and an equal amount of floss. His younger brother asked for a quarter to pay their state tribute. He gave it all without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 初布魯海牙拜廉使，命下之日，子希憲適生，喜曰：「吾聞古以官為姓，天其以廉為吾宗之姓乎！」

translations.literal: When Buluhaiya was first appointed surveillance commissioner, on the day the order was issued his son Xixian was just born; he rejoiced and said, “I have heard that in antiquity men took office as surname—might Heaven take Lian as our clan’s surname!
translations.idiomatic: When Buluhaiya was first appointed surveillance commissioner, his son Xixian was born that very day. He rejoiced and said, “I have heard that in antiquity men took their office as their surname. Perhaps Heaven means our clan to be surnamed Lian!

sentences.zh: 故子孫皆姓廉氏。

translations.literal: Therefore descendants all took the surname Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his descendants all bore the surname Lian.

sentences.zh: 後或奏廉氏仕進者多，宜稍汰去，世祖曰：「布魯海牙功多，子孫亦朕所知，非汝當預。」

translations.literal: Later someone memorialized that many of the Lian clan had entered office and they should be somewhat weeded out; Shizu said, “Buluhaiya’s merit is great, and his descendants are also known to me—this is not for you to interfere in.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone memorialized that too many of the Lian clan held office and some should be removed. Kublai said, “Buluhaiya’s service was great, and I know his descendants. This is not your concern.

sentences.zh: 大德初，贈儀同三司、大司徒，追封魏國公，諡孝懿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dade he was posthumously given Grand Master of the Palace Equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Minister of Education, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with posthumous title Filial and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dade reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Master Equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous title Filial and Kind.

sentences.zh: 子希閔、希憲、希恕、希尹、希顏、希愿、希魯、希貢、希中、希括，孫五十三人，登顯仕者代有之，希憲自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Ximin, Xixian, Xishu, Xiyin, Xiyan, Xiyuan, Xilu, Xigong, Xizhong, and Xikuo; fifty-three grandsons; those who reached eminent office appeared in every generation; Xixian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ximin, Xixian, Xishu, Xiyin, Xiyan, Xiyuan, Xilu, Xigong, Xizhong, and Xikuo. He had fifty-three grandsons, and eminent office ran in the family for generations. Xixian has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 高智耀子睿附

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao—his son Rui appended
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhiyao—with his son Rui appended

sentences.zh: 高智耀，河西人，世仕夏國。

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao was a man of Hexi; for generations his family served the Xia state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhiyao was from Hexi. His family had served the Western Xia for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖逸，大都督府尹；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was Director of the Great Capital Military Commission;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi was Director of the Great Capital Military Commission;

sentences.zh: 祖良惠，右丞相。

translations.literal: his grandfather Lianghui was Right Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: and his grandfather Lianghui was Right Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 智耀登本國進士第，夏亡，隱賀蘭山。

translations.literal: Zhiyao passed his state’s jinshi examination; when Xia perished, he hid on Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyao passed the jinshi examination of his state. When the Xia fell, he withdrew to Mount Helan.

sentences.zh: 太宗訪求河西故家子孫之賢者，衆以智耀對，召見將用之，遽辭歸。

translations.literal: Taizong sought out worthy descendants of old Hexi families; the multitude answered with Zhiyao; he was summoned and about to be employed, but he abruptly declined and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei sought worthy descendants of old Hexi families. Zhiyao was recommended, summoned, and about to be appointed, but he declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 皇子闊端鎮西涼，儒者皆隸役，智耀謁藩邸，言儒者給復已久，一旦與冢養同役，非便，請除之。

translations.literal: Prince Kuoduan was stationed in Xiliang; Confucian scholars were all assigned to corvée; Zhiyao visited the princely residence and said that scholars had long enjoyed exemption, yet suddenly to share corvée with tomb-service households was not convenient—he requested their removal from it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuoduan governed Xiliang, where Confucian scholars had been put to corvée labor. Zhiyao visited the prince and argued that scholars had long enjoyed tax exemption and should not suddenly be yoked to corvée alongside common households. He asked that the practice be ended.

sentences.zh: 皇子從其言。

translations.literal: The prince followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 欲奏官之，不就。

translations.literal: He wished to memorialize to appoint him to office, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to recommend him for office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，智耀入見，言：「儒者所學堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之道，自古有國家者，用之則治，不用則否，養成其材，將以資其用也。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, Zhiyao entered audience and said, “What Confucian scholars study is the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; since antiquity states that employed it were governed, those that did not were not; nurturing their talent is to supply their employment.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke ascended the throne, Zhiyao came to court and said, “Confucian scholars study the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Throughout history states that employed them prospered and those that did not declined. Their training is meant to supply the state with talent.

sentences.zh: 宜蠲免徭役以教育之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to remit corvée and levies in order to educate them.
translations.idiomatic: They should be exempted from corvée so they may be properly educated.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「儒家何如巫醫？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked, “How do Confucians compare to shamans and physicians?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “How do Confucians compare to shamans and physicians?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「儒以綱常治天下，豈方技所得比。」

translations.literal: He replied, “Confucians govern all under Heaven through the constant bonds—how can they be compared with technical specialists.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, “Confucians govern the realm through moral principle. How can they be compared with mere technicians?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: The emperor said, “Good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Well said.

sentences.zh: 前此未有以是告朕者。」

translations.literal: Before this no one had told me this.
translations.idiomatic: No one had ever told me this before.

sentences.zh: 詔復海內儒士徭役，無有所與。

translations.literal: An edict restored corvée exemption for Confucian scholars throughout the realm, with none to share in it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored corvée exemption for Confucian scholars throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸已聞其賢，及即位，召見，又力言儒術有補治道，反覆辯論，辭累千百。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in his princely residence he had already heard of his worth; when he took the throne he summoned him; again he forcefully argued that Confucian learning supplements the way of governance, debating back and forth, his words numbering thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had heard of his worth while still heir apparent. After his accession he summoned him. Zhiyao argued forcefully that Confucian learning was essential to good government, debating at length in thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 帝異其言，鑄印授之，命凡免役儒戶，皆從之給公文為左驗。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his words, cast a seal and bestowed it on him, and ordered that for all exempt scholar households, documents should be issued from him as verification on the left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed, had a seal cast and entrusted to him, and ordered that all exempt scholar households receive official documents from him as proof.

sentences.zh: 時淮、蜀士遭俘虜者，皆沒為奴，智耀奏言：「以儒為驅，古無有也。

translations.literal: At that time scholars of Huai and Shu who had been taken captive were all enslaved; Zhiyao memorialized, saying, “To make Confucians into servants—there is no such thing in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars captured in the Huai and Shu regions had been enslaved. Zhiyao memorialized, “To use scholars as slaves has no precedent in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 陛下方以古道為治，宜除之，以風厲天下。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now governing by the ancient Way—it is fitting to remove this, to admonish and encourage all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs by the ancient Way. This practice should be abolished to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，即拜翰林學士，命循行郡縣區別之，得數千人。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; he was at once appointed Hanlin Academician and ordered to travel through commanderies and counties to distinguish them, obtaining several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, appointed him Hanlin Academician, and sent him through the commanderies and counties to identify scholars. Several thousand were recovered.

sentences.zh: 貴臣或言其詭濫，帝詰之，對曰：「士，譬則金也，金色有淺深，謂之非金不可，才藝有淺深，謂之非士亦不可。」

translations.literal: Noble ministers sometimes said his list was deceitful and excessive; the emperor questioned him; he replied, “Scholars are like gold: gold’s color has depth and shallowness—one cannot say it is not gold; talent and learning have depth and shallowness—one cannot say they are not scholars either.
translations.idiomatic: Some nobles accused him of padding the rolls. The emperor questioned him. He replied, “Scholars are like gold: gold varies in purity, yet it is still gold. Talent varies in depth, yet the men are still scholars.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，更寵賚之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and further favored and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded him further.

sentences.zh: 智耀又言：「國初庶政草創，綱紀未張，宜倣前代，置御史臺以糾肅官常。」

translations.literal: Zhiyao also said, “At the founding of the state numerous affairs were newly begun and statutes not yet extended—it is fitting to imitate former dynasties and establish a Censorate to rectify and discipline official conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyao also argued that in the founding years government was still being organized and discipline was lax. Following former dynasties, a Censorate should be established to enforce official conduct.

sentences.zh: 至元五年立御史臺，用其議也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the Censorate was established—his proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was established in Zhiyuan 5 on his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 擢西夏中興等路提刑按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner for Punishments of Zhongxing and other routes in Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner for Punishments of Zhongxing and other routes in Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 會西北藩王遣使入朝，謂：「本朝舊俗與漢法異，今留漢地，建都邑城郭，儀文制度，遵用漢法，其故何如？」

translations.literal: It happened that a northwestern prince sent envoys to court, saying, “Our dynasty’s old customs differ from Han law; now you remain in Han lands, build capitals, cities, and walls, and in ritual, script, and institutions follow Han law—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: A northwestern prince sent envoys to court who asked, “Your dynasty’s customs differ from Han law. Why do you now remain in Han territory, build cities and walls, and adopt Han ritual and institutions?

sentences.zh: 帝求報聘之使以析其問，智耀入見，請行，帝問所荅，畫一敷對，稱旨，即日遣就道。

translations.literal: The emperor sought a return envoy to analyze their questions; Zhiyao entered audience and requested to go; the emperor asked what he would answer; he laid out replies one by one; it matched the emperor’s intent, and that same day he was dispatched on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sought an envoy to answer them. Zhiyao volunteered, outlined his replies point by point, and pleased the emperor. He was sent on his way that same day.

sentences.zh: 至上京，病卒，帝為之震悼。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangjing, he died of illness; the emperor was shaken with grief for him.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Shangjing but died of illness on the way. The emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 後贈崇文贊治功臣、金紫光祿大夫、司徒、柱國，追封寧國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given the title Merit Subject Who Honors Culture and Assists in Ordering, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ning, with posthumous title Cultured and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as Merit Subject Who Honors Culture and Assists in Ordering, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ning, with the posthumous title Cultured and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子睿。

translations.literal: His son Rui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rui.

sentences.zh: 睿，資稟直亮，智耀之北使也，攜之以行。

translations.literal: Rui’s endowment was upright and bright; when Zhiyao went as envoy northward, he took him along.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was upright by nature. When Zhiyao went on his northern mission he took his son with him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝問其子安在，近臣以睿見，時年十六。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor asked where his son was; a close minister presented Rui—he was then sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor asked after his son. A close minister presented Rui, then sixteen years old.

sentences.zh: 授符寶郎，出入禁闥，恭謹詳雅。

translations.literal: He was appointed Keeper of Seals and Credentials, entering and leaving the forbidden apartments, respectful, prudent, detailed, and refined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Keeper of Seals and Credentials and admitted to the inner palace, where he conducted himself with respectful precision.

sentences.zh: 久之，授唐兀衛指揮副使，歷翰林待制、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Vice Commander of the Tangut Guard, and served as Hanlin Attendant Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became Vice Commander of the Tangut Guard, then served as Hanlin Attendant Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 除嘉興路緫管，境內有宿盜，白晝掠民財，捕者積十數輩莫敢近。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Administrator of Jiaxing Route; within the territory were long-standing bandits who plundered commoners’ property in broad daylight; accumulations of more than ten pursuers did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: As chief administrator of Jiaxing Route he faced veteran bandits who robbed in broad daylight. Pursuers in groups of ten or more dared not approach them.

sentences.zh: 睿下令，不旬日，生擒之，一郡以寧。

translations.literal: Rui issued orders; within ten days he captured them alive, and the whole commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rui issued orders, and within ten days they were captured alive. The entire commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 擢江東道提刑按察使，部內草竊陸梁，聲言圍宣城，郡將怯懦，城門不開，睿召責之曰：「寇勢方熾，官先示弱，民何所憑。」

translations.literal: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner for Punishments of the Jiangdong Circuit; within his jurisdiction grass bandits were unruly; rumor said they would besiege Xuancheng; the commandery general was cowardly and would not open the city gates; Rui summoned and rebuked him, saying, “The bandits’ power is just now fierce—if officials first show weakness, on what can the people rely?
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Surveillance Commissioner for Punishments of the Jiangdong Circuit, he found bandits rampant and rumors that Xuancheng would be besieged. The commandery general, timid, kept the gates closed. Rui summoned and rebuked him: “The bandits are at their height. If officials show fear first, what hope have the people?

sentences.zh: 即命密治兵衛，而洞開城門，聽民出入貿易自便。

translations.literal: He at once ordered troops and guards prepared in secret, yet threw open the city gates wide and allowed the people to come and go and trade as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly prepared the garrison but threw the gates wide open and let the people come and go and trade freely.

sentences.zh: 既而寇以有備，不敢進，遂討平之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits, seeing preparations in place, did not dare advance, and he then campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city prepared, the bandits did not dare advance, and he soon suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 除同僉行樞密院事，遷浙西道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and transferred to Purification Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and transferred to Purification Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鹽官州民，有連結黨與，持郡邑短長，其目曰十老，吏莫敢問，睿悉按以法，闔境快之。

translations.literal: In Yan’guan Prefecture commoners had formed linked factions who held the commandery and district’s strengths and weaknesses; they were called the Ten Elders; clerks did not dare investigate; Rui prosecuted them all according to law, and the whole territory rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan’guan Prefecture factions called the Ten Elders controlled local affairs and intimidated officials. Rui prosecuted them all by law, to the relief of the entire region.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行臺侍御史，進御史中丞，除淮東道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, advanced to Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Purification Commissioner of the Huaidong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, promoted to Censor-in-Chief, and made Purification Commissioner of the Huaidong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 盜竊真州庫鈔三萬緡，有司大索，追逮平民數百人，吏因為奸利，睿躬自詳讞而得其情，即縱遣之。

translations.literal: Bandits stole thirty thousand strings of paper money from Zhenzhou’s treasury; responsible offices searched broadly and pursued and seized several hundred commoners; clerks thereby made illicit profit; Rui personally conducted detailed judgment and obtained the true facts, and at once released and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves stole thirty thousand strings of paper money from the Zhenzhou treasury. Officials rounded up hundreds of innocent civilians while clerks profited from the investigation. Rui personally tried the cases, found the truth, and released them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，果得真盜。

translations.literal: Before long the true bandits were indeed obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the real thieves were caught.

sentences.zh: 復拜南臺御史中丞，務持大體，有儒者之風焉。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate, devoted to upholding the larger pattern, and had the bearing of a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate, upholding broad principles in the manner of a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年卒，年六十有六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanyou 1 at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 累贈推忠佐理功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封寧國公，諡貞簡。

translations.literal: Cumulatively he was posthumously given the title Merit Subject Who Sincerely Assists in Ordering, Grand Tutor, Grand Master with privilege of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ning, with posthumous title Upright and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Merit Subject Who Sincerely Assists in Ordering, Grand Tutor, with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and Duke of Ning, with the posthumous title Upright and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子納麟，官至太尉、江南諸道行御史臺大夫。

translations.literal: His son Nalin, in office reached Grand Marshal and Grand Coordinator of the Branch Censorate for all Jiangnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nalin rose to Grand Marshal and Grand Coordinator of the Branch Censorate for all Jiangnan circuits.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥，姓伽乃氏，迦葉彌兒人。

translations.literal: Tiege, surname Clan Ganaishi, a man of Kasmira.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege, of the Ganaishi clan, was a native of Kasmira.

sentences.zh: 迦葉彌兒者，西域築乾國也。

translations.literal: Kasmira is the Western Regions’ state of Zhugan.
translations.idiomatic: Kasmira was the Western Region state known as Zhugan.

sentences.zh: 父斡脫赤與叔父那摩俱學浮屠氏。
