translations.literal: His father Otuchi and his uncle Namo both studied the Buddhist teachings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Otuchi and his uncle Namo both studied Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 斡脫赤兄弟相謂曰：「世道擾攘，吾國將亡，東北有天子氣，盍往歸之。」

translations.literal: The brothers Otuchi said to one another, “The age is turbulent and our state is about to perish; in the northeast there is the aura of a Son of Heaven—why not go and submit to him?
translations.idiomatic: Otuchi and his brothers said to one another, “The world is in turmoil and our country is doomed. There is imperial destiny in the northeast—let us go and submit.

sentences.zh: 乃偕入見，太宗禮遇之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went together to audience; Taizong treated them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: They went together to audience, and Ögedei received them with honor.

sentences.zh: 定宗師事那摩，以斡脫赤佩金符，奉使省民瘼。

translations.literal: Dingzong honored Namo as teacher; Otuchi wore the golden tally and was sent as envoy to investigate the people’s afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong honored Namo as his teacher and sent Otuchi, bearing a golden tally, as envoy to inquire into the people’s hardships.

sentences.zh: 憲宗尊那摩為國師，授玉印，緫天下釋教。

translations.literal: Xianzong honored Namo as National Preceptor, bestowed a jade seal, and placed him over all Buddhist teaching under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke honored Namo as National Preceptor, granted him a jade seal, and placed him over all Buddhist clergy in the realm.

sentences.zh: 斡脫赤亦貴用事，領迦葉彌兒萬戶，奏曰：「迦葉彌兒西陲小國，尚未臣服，請往諭之。」

translations.literal: Otuchi also became noble and wielded power, heading the Kasmira myriarchy; he memorialized, saying, “Kasmira is a small state on the western border and has not yet submitted—please let me go to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Otuchi also rose to power as head of the Kasmira myriarchy. He memorialized, “Kasmira is a small border state that has not yet submitted. Allow me to go and persuade them.

sentences.zh: 詔偕近侍以往。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to go together with close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to go with imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 其國主不從，怒而殺之，帝為發兵誅國主。

translations.literal: The state’s lord would not obey, and in anger killed him; the emperor sent troops to execute the state lord.
translations.idiomatic: The local ruler refused and killed him in anger. The emperor sent troops to execute the ruler.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年封代國公，諡忠遂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, with posthumous title Loyal and Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, with the title Loyal and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 先是，世祖事憲宗甚親愛，後以讒稍疏，國師導世祖宜加敬慎，遂友愛如初。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shizu served Xianzong with great intimacy and affection; later, because of slander, they grew somewhat distant; the National Preceptor guided Shizu to add respect and caution, and they became friendly and loving as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kublai had been very close to Möngke, but slander later drove them apart. The National Preceptor advised Kublai to show greater respect and caution, and the brothers were reconciled.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝將用鐵哥，曰：「吾以酬國師也。」

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was about to employ Tiege and said, “I do this to repay the National Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to employ Tiege he said, “I do this to repay the National Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 於是鐵哥年十七，詔擇貴家女妻之，辭曰：「臣母漢人，每欲求漢人女為婦，臣不敢傷母心。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Tiege was seventeen; an edict chose a noble family’s daughter to be his wife; he declined, saying, “My mother is Han; she always wished for a Han woman as daughter-in-law—I dare not wound my mother’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege was then seventeen. The court chose a noble family’s daughter for his wife, but he declined: “My mother is Han and has always wanted a Han daughter-in-law. I dare not disappoint her.

sentences.zh: 乃為娶冉氏女。

translations.literal: He was then given a woman of the Ran clan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a woman of the Ran clan in marriage instead.

sentences.zh: 久之，命掌饔膳湯藥，日益親密。

translations.literal: After a long time he was ordered to manage meals and medicinal broths, and day by day grew more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was put in charge of the imperial meals and medicines and grew ever closer to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，鐵哥奏曰：「武臣佩符，古制也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan Tiege memorialized, saying, “For military officers to wear tallies is ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 16 Tiege memorialized, “Military officers wearing tallies is an ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 今長民者亦佩符，請省之，以彰武職。」

translations.literal: Now those who govern the people also wear tallies—please reduce this to make martial office manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Now civil administrators also wear them. Please abolish this practice to distinguish military rank.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進正議大夫、尚膳監。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Grand Master of Correct Counsel and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Counsel and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭之曰：「朕聞父飲藥，子先嘗之，君飲藥，臣先嘗之。

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed him, saying, “I have heard that when a father drinks medicine, the son tastes it first; when a lord drinks medicine, the minister tastes it first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, “I have heard that when a father takes medicine the son tastes it first, and when a ruler takes medicine the minister tastes it first.

sentences.zh: 今卿典朕膳，凡飲食湯藥，宜先嘗之。」

translations.literal: Now you oversee my meals—all food, drink, and medicinal broths—you should taste them first.
translations.idiomatic: You oversee my meals. All food, drink, and medicines should be tasted by you first.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕以宿衛士隸卿，其可任使者，疏其才能，朕將用之。」

translations.literal: He also said, “I assign palace guards to your command; those who can be sent on missions—set forth their abilities in a memorial, and I will employ them.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “I assign palace guards to you. Report the abilities of those fit for service, and I will employ them.

sentences.zh: 詔賜第於大明宮之左，留守段圭言：「逼木局，不便。」

translations.literal: An edict granted a residence to the left of the Daming Palace; the garrison commander Duan Gui said, “It presses against the timber office—this is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a residence east of the Daming Palace. The garrison commander Duan Gui objected that it was too close to the timber office and inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「俾居近禁闥，以便召使。

translations.literal: The emperor said, “Let him dwell near the forbidden apartments so he may be summoned conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Let him live near the inner palace so I may summon him easily.

sentences.zh: 木局稍隘，又何害焉。」

translations.literal: The timber office is slightly cramped—what harm is there in that?”
translations.idiomatic: The timber office is a bit cramped. What harm is there in that?”

sentences.zh: 高州人言，州境多野獸害稼，願捕以充貢。

translations.literal: Men of Gaozhou said that within the prefecture many wild beasts harmed the crops and they wished to hunt them to fulfill tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Gaozhou reported that wild beasts were damaging crops and asked permission to hunt them for tribute.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「捕獸充貢，徒濟其私耳，且擾民，不可聽。」

translations.literal: Tiege said, “Hunting beasts to fulfill tribute only serves private gain, and moreover disturbs the people—it must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Hunting for tribute would only serve private interests and disturb the people. It must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遷同知宣徽院事，領尚膳監。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Associate Director of the Palace Provisionery and headed the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became Associate Director of the Palace Provisionery while retaining charge of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 有食尚食餘餅者，帝察知之，怒。

translations.literal: Someone ate leftover cakes from the imperial kitchen; the emperor detected it and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Someone was found eating leftover cakes from the imperial kitchen. The emperor discovered it and was furious.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「失餅之罪在臣，食者何與焉。」

translations.literal: Tiege said, “The fault of losing the cakes lies with me—what have the eaters to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “The fault for the lost cakes is mine. What have the eaters to do with it?

sentences.zh: 內府食用圓米，鐵哥奏曰：「計粳米一石，僅得圓米四斗，請自今非御用，止給常米。」

translations.literal: The inner palace used polished round rice; Tiege memorialized, saying, “Calculating from one shi of husked rice, one obtains only four dou of round rice—from now on, for what is not imperial use, please give only ordinary rice.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace used polished round rice. Tiege memorialized that one shi of husked rice yielded only four dou of polished rice, and asked that ordinary rice be supplied except for imperial use.

sentences.zh: 帝皆善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 進中奉大夫、司農寺達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Darughachi of the Ministry of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Darughachi of the Ministry of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 從獵百杳兒之地，獵人亦不剌金射兔，誤中名駝，駝死，帝怒，命誅之。

translations.literal: Following the hunt at Bainao’er, the hunter Yibulajin shot at a rabbit, mistakenly struck a famous camel, and the camel died; the emperor was angry and ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Bainao’er the hunter Yibulajin shot at a rabbit but accidentally killed a prized camel. The emperor was furious and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「殺人償畜，刑太重。」

translations.literal: Tiege said, “To kill a man to repay a beast—the punishment is too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Executing a man for killing a beast is too severe a penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「 誤耶，史官必書。」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said, “A mistake? The historiographers will surely record it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, “A mistake? The historiographers will surely record this.

sentences.zh: 亟釋之。

translations.literal: He at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the man released.

sentences.zh: 庾人有盜鑿秔米者，罪當死。

translations.literal: A granary keeper stole non-glutinous rice by breaking into the stores; the offense merited death.
translations.idiomatic: A granary keeper who broke into the stores and stole rice was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥諫曰：「臣鞫庾人，其母病，盜秔欲食母耳，請貸之。」

translations.literal: Tiege remonstrated, saying, "When I examined the granary keeper, his mother was ill; he stole the rice only because he wished to feed his mother. Please pardon him."
translations.idiomatic: Tiege remonstrated, "On investigation I found his mother was ill, and he stole the rice only to feed her. I beg that he be spared."

sentences.zh: 牧人有盜割駝峰者，將誅之。

translations.literal: A herdsman had stolen and cut off a camel’s hump and was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: A herdsman who had cut a hump from a living camel was about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「生割駝峰，誠忍人也。

translations.literal: Tiege said, “To cut a camel’s hump while it lives—he is indeed a cruel man.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “To cut a hump from a living camel is indeed cruel.

sentences.zh: 然殺之，恐乖陛下仁恕心。」

translations.literal: Yet to kill him may go against Your Majesty’s heart of benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to execute him may go against Your Majesty’s merciful nature.

sentences.zh: 詔皆免死。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them all from death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared them all.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進正奉大夫，奏：「司農寺宜陞為大司農司，秩二品，使天下知朝廷重農之意。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was advanced to Grand Master of Correct Submission and memorialized: “The Ministry of Agriculture should be promoted to the Grand Ministry of Agriculture, rank second grade, so that all under Heaven may know the court’s intent to honor agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Submission and memorialized that the Ministry of Agriculture should be elevated to the Grand Ministry of Agriculture, second rank, so the realm would know the court valued farming.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The regulation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 進資善大夫、司農。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Assisting Goodness and Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Goodness and Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時司農供膳，有司多擾民，鐵哥奏曰：「屯田則備諸物，立供膳司甚便。」

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Agriculture supplied meals; responsible offices often disturbed the people; Tiege memorialized, saying, “Garrison fields can prepare all goods—establishing a Provisionery for Meals would be very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Agriculture supplied the court’s meals, and local offices often harassed the people. Tiege proposed that garrison fields supply provisions and that a separate Provisionery for Meals be established.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 桓州饑民鬻子女以為食，鐵哥奏以官帑贖之。

translations.literal: Famine-stricken people of Huanzhou sold sons and daughters for food; Tiege memorialized to redeem them with government funds.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people in Huanzhou were selling their children for food. Tiege memorialized to redeem them with government funds.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征乃顏，至撒兒都之地，叛王塔不台率兵奄至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the campaign against Nayan; reaching the place of Sa’erdu, the rebel prince Tabutai led troops that suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he accompanied the campaign against Nayan. At Sa’erdu the rebel prince Tabutai suddenly appeared with his army.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥奏曰：「昔李廣一將耳，尚能以疑退敵，況陛下萬乘之威乎。

translations.literal: Tiege memorialized, saying, “In the past Li Guang was but one general, yet he could still use doubt to repel the enemy—how much more Your Majesty’s majesty of ten thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Li Guang was only a single general, yet he once repelled the enemy through deception. How much more can Your Majesty’s imperial majesty do so!

sentences.zh: 今彼衆我寡，不得地利，當設疑以退之。」

translations.literal: Now they are many and we few, without favorable terrain—we should set up deception to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us and we lack favorable ground. We should use deception to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 於是帝張曲蓋，據胡床，鐵哥從容進酒。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor spread a curved canopy, sat on a barbarian chair, and Tiege at ease advanced wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then raised his canopy, sat on a camp chair, and Tiege calmly served him wine.

sentences.zh: 塔不台按兵覘伺，懼有伏，遂引去。

translations.literal: Tabutai held his troops and watched; fearing an ambush, he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tabutai halted his troops to observe, feared an ambush, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝以金章宗玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on him the jade belt of the Jin emperor Zhangzong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with the jade belt of the Jin emperor Zhangzong.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，進榮祿大夫、中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was advanced to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以病足，聽輿轎入殿門。

translations.literal: Because his feet were ill, he was permitted to enter the palace gate in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness in his feet he was permitted to enter the palace gate in a litter.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗憶北征事，不能悉記，鐵哥條舉甚詳，帝悅，以金束帶賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor once recalled the northern campaign but could not remember it fully; Tiege listed items in great detail; the emperor was pleased and bestowed a gold belt on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor tried to recall the northern campaign but could not remember all the details, Tiege recounted them at length. The emperor was pleased and gave him a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 初，詔遣宋新附民種蒲萄於野馬川晃火兒不剌之地，既獻其實，鐵哥以北方多寒，奏歲賜衣服，從之。

translations.literal: Initially an edict sent newly submitted people of Song to plant grapes at Yemachuan in Huanghu’erbula; when they presented the fruit, Tiege, because the north was mostly cold, memorialized for annual grants of clothing, and it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had sent newly submitted Song subjects to plant grapes at Yemachuan in Huanghu’erbula. When they presented the harvest, Tiege noted the cold of the north and memorialized for annual grants of clothing, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，以鐵哥先朝舊臣，賜銀一千兩、鈔十萬貫。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, because Tiege was an old minister of the former court, he was granted one thousand taels of silver and one hundred thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne he rewarded Tiege, an old minister of the previous reign, with one thousand taels of silver and one hundred thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 他日，又賜以瑪瑙碗，謂鐵哥曰：「此器先皇所用，朕今賜卿，以卿久侍先皇故也。」

translations.literal: Another day he again bestowed an agate bowl and told Tiege, “This vessel was used by the late emperor; I now grant it to you because you long served the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he gave him an agate bowl and said, “This vessel was used by my father. I give it to you because you long served him.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was given Grand Master of Glorious Blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing.

sentences.zh: 三年，乞解機務，從之。

translations.literal: In the third year he begged to be released from state affairs; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he asked to retire from active administration, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 仍授平章政事、議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was still appointed Grand Councillor and deliberator on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was nevertheless retained as Grand Councillor with authority to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 時諸王朝見，未有知典故者，帝曰：「惟鐵哥知之，俾專其事，凡廩餼金帛之數，皆遵世祖制詔，自今懷諸王之禮，悉命鐵哥掌之。」

translations.literal: At that time when the princes came to court audience, none knew ceremonial precedents; the emperor said, “Only Tiege knows them—have him specialize in these matters; all quantities of grain stipends, gold, and silks shall follow Shizu’s regulations and edicts; from now on the rites for receiving the princes—all are ordered to be managed by Tiege.”
translations.idiomatic: When the princes came to court none knew the ceremonial precedents. The emperor said, “Only Tiege knows them. Let him handle these matters. All stipends of grain, gold, and silk shall follow Kublai’s regulations. From now on the rites for receiving the princes shall all be managed by Tiege.”

sentences.zh: 七年，復拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 平灤大水，鐵哥奏曰：「散財聚民，古之道也。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Pingluan; Tiege memorialized, saying, “To disperse wealth and gather the people is the ancient Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingluan suffered severe flooding, Tiege memorialized, “Dispersing wealth to gather the people is the ancient Way.

sentences.zh: 今平灤水災，不加賑恤，民不聊生矣！」

translations.literal: Now Pingluan’s flood disaster—if relief is not added, the people will have no livelihood!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pingluan has received no relief. The people cannot survive!

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was ordered.

sentences.zh: 十年，丁母憂，詔奪情起復。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered mourning for his mother; an edict seized his grief and recalled him to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died. He was ordered to leave mourning and return to office.

sentences.zh: 遼王脫脫入朝，從者執兵入大明宮，鐵哥劾止之，王懼謝。

translations.literal: The Liao prince Tuohuatuo entered court audience; followers bearing weapons entered the Daming Palace; Tiege impeached and stopped them; the prince feared and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao prince Tuohuatuo came to court his attendants entered the Daming Palace armed. Tiege impeached them and stopped it. The prince apologized in fear.

sentences.zh: 從幸縉山，饑民相望，鐵哥輒發廩賑之，既乃陳疏自劾，帝稱善不已。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Jinyun, famine victims stretched as far as one could see; Tiege repeatedly opened granaries to relieve them; afterward he submitted a memorial impeaching himself; the emperor praised him without end.
translations.idiomatic: On an excursion to Jinyun he saw famine victims everywhere and repeatedly opened granaries to feed them. He then memorialized impeaching himself for overstepping. The emperor praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，賜金一百兩，加金紫光祿大夫，遙授中書右丞相。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, he was granted one hundred taels of gold, advanced to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and appointed from afar as Right Chief Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne he was granted one hundred taels of gold, promoted to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and appointed Right Chief Councillor of the Secretariat in absentia.

sentences.zh: 有訴寧遠王闊闊出有逆謀者，命誅之。

translations.literal: Someone accused the Prince of Ningyuan, Kuokuochu, of plotting rebellion; an order was given to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Prince Kuokuochu of Ningyuan of plotting rebellion, and an order was issued for his execution.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥知其誣，廷辨之，由是得釋，徙高麗。

translations.literal: Tiege knew it was false accusation and argued in court; thereby he was released and was transferred to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege knew the charge was false and argued the case at court. The prince was released and exiled to Korea.

sentences.zh: 二年，領度支院。

translations.literal: In the second year he headed the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he headed the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋賜江州稻田五千畝。

translations.literal: Shortly he was granted five thousand mu of paddy fields in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted five thousand mu of paddy fields in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子六人：忽察，淮東宣慰使；

translations.literal: He had six sons: Hucha, Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Hucha, Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong;

sentences.zh: 平安奴，太平路達魯花赤；

translations.literal: Ping’annu, Darughachi of Taiping Route;
translations.idiomatic: Ping’annu, Darughachi of Taiping Route;

sentences.zh: 也識哥，同知山東宣慰司事；

translations.literal: Yeshige, Associate Director of the Shandong Pacification Commission;
translations.idiomatic: Yeshige, Associate Director of the Shandong Pacification Commission;

sentences.zh: 虎里台，同知真定緫管府事；

translations.literal: Hulitai, Associate Administrator of the Zhending Chief Administration;
translations.idiomatic: Hulitai, Associate Administrator of the Zhending Chief Administration;

sentences.zh: 亦可麻，同知都護府事；

translations.literal: Yikema, Associate Administrator of the Protectorate General;
translations.idiomatic: Yikema, Associate Administrator of the Protectorate General;

sentences.zh: 重喜，隆禧院副使。

translations.literal: Chongxi, Vice Commissioner of the Longxi Court.
translations.idiomatic: and Chongxi, Vice Commissioner of the Longxi Court.

sentences.zh: 孫八人，伯顏，中書平章政事，餘多居宿衛。

translations.literal: He had eight grandsons; Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat; the rest mostly served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight grandsons, including Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat; most of the others served in the palace guard.
